memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is the account of the family line of Abraham's son Isaac. Abraham became the father of Isaac, and Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram and sister of Laban the Aramean. Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was childless. The LORD answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant." - Gen 25:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isaac married at forty, and we soon learn that Rebekah was unable to have children. Here was the son of promise — through whom God had said a great nation would come — and yet his wife was barren. The promise seemed stuck.

What does Isaac do? He prays. He takes the very problem that threatens the promise and brings it to the Lord. And notice the tender detail: he prayed "on behalf of his wife." He carried Rebekah's sorrow as his own and interceded for her.

But this was no instant answer. Compare the ages: Isaac was forty at his marriage and sixty when the twins were born (v.26). That means about twenty years of praying and waiting. Twenty years! Isaac kept bringing the same request to God, year after year, until the answer came.

If you are waiting on God for something — a child, a breakthrough, a healing, a change — take heart from Isaac. Long delays are not proof that God has forgotten. Keep praying. Keep trusting. God's timing is not our timing, but His answers are worth the wait. The Lord who answered Isaac still hears the persistent prayers of His children (Luke 18:1).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I stopped praying about because the wait felt too long?
2. Am I, like Isaac, willing to carry others' burdens in prayer?
3. How can I keep trusting God's timing when answers are slow?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the patience to keep praying through long seasons of waiting. Help me to trust that You hear me and will answer in Your perfect time. Amen.
